scope: Proposition 7.2 (Exact relative Morava descent) of the manuscript “The height-three chromatic overlap: an explicit filtration and its attachments” (preprints/The-height-three-chromatic-overlap-an-explicit-filtration-and-its-attachments-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 318 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 05577ee22db5cad1), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 56. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let n ≥ 1, let k be a finite field containing F = Fpn , and let Rn,k = LK(n)Sk. In the K(n)-local category of Sk-modules, the algebra En(k) is descendable over the unit Rn,k. Write b ⊗ for the tensor product in this local category and put Nq n = En(k) b ⊗Rn,k (q+1) (q ≥ 0). Its augmented Amitsur object totalizes to Rn,k. Every exact functor from this local category to a stable category preserves that totalization and a uniform nilpotence bound for its error tower. In particular this applies to the inclusion in spectra followed by ordinary smash, a finite Moore quotient, a chromatic localization, or a monochromatic fiber. There are identifications of graded rings π∗Nq n ∼ = Ccts(Pq n, En(k)∗), (7.2) with the maximal-ideal topology on the coefficients. Under these identifications the actual cofaces and codegeneracies induce those of the continuous action cobar construction, and the augmented unit is the constant unit. Each Nq n is an ordinary En(k)-module through its first factor. This is the module structure used when an ordinary exact functor is applied to a term.
